017package org.apache.juneau.rest.server.filter;
018
019import static org.apache.juneau.commons.utils.Shorts.*;
020
021import java.nio.charset.*;
022import java.security.*;
023import java.util.*;
024
025import javax.crypto.*;
026import javax.crypto.spec.*;
027
028import jakarta.servlet.http.*;
029
030/**
031 * Where a CSRF synchronizer token comes from, and how it is masked for embedding and checked on the way back.
032 *
033 * <p>
034 * Two strategies are available:
035 * <ul>
036 *    <li>{@link #perSession()} &mdash; the default.  The token is <c>HMAC-SHA256(key, UTF-8(sessionId))</c>, so
037 *       every session has its own token and nothing is stored in the session.  An attacker who can load the page
038 *       in their own browser learns only their own token, never the victim's.
039 *    <li>{@link #perProcess()} / {@link #perProcess(SynchronizerToken)} &mdash; one token for the whole process.
040 *       It needs no session, but any visitor can read it, so in a multi-user application it adds little beyond
041 *       the <c>Origin</c> check.
042 * </ul>
043 *
044 * <h5 class='section'>Masking</h5>
045 * <p>
046 * The value written into a page is never the token itself.  Each embed gets a fresh 32-byte pad, and the
047 * published value is <c>hex(pad || (pad XOR token))</c>: 128 lower-case hex characters.  The secret therefore
048 * never repeats across renders or across the several places one page embeds it, which defeats an HTML
049 * compression oracle (BREACH).  That is <b>all</b> masking buys: anyone who sees the wire value can unmask it, so
050 * the token header must never be logged, and masking gives no protection to logs, proxies or the browser.
051 *
052 * <h5 class='section'>Verification</h5>
053 * <p>
054 * A presented value must be exactly 128 lower-case hex characters; anything else is refused before the secret is
055 * touched.  It is then unmasked and compared with {@link MessageDigest#isEqual(byte[], byte[])} against the
056 * expected 32 bytes.  A request with no session is compared against the HMAC of a fixed placeholder id that no
057 * container can issue, so "no session" and "wrong token" do the same work and give the same answer.
058 *
059 * <h5 class='section'>Session ids</h5>
060 * <p>
061 * A per-session token changes whenever the session id changes, and this class never changes it.  An application
062 * must call {@link HttpServletRequest#changeSessionId()} on login; otherwise a token seen before login stays
063 * valid after it.
064 *
065 * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
066 * <p class='bjava'>
067 *    <jc>// Default: one token per session, keyed by 32 fresh random bytes for this process.</jc>
068 *    CsrfTokens <jv>tokens</jv> = CsrfTokens.<jsm>perSession</jsm>();
069 *
070 *    <jc>// A cluster: every node shares one CSPRNG-generated key, so any node accepts any node's token.</jc>
071 *    CsrfTokens <jv>clustered</jv> = CsrfTokens.<jsm>perSession</jsm>().key(<jv>keyBytesFromSecretStore</jv>);
072 * </p>
073 *
074 * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
075 *    <li class='jc'>{@link SynchronizerToken}
076 * </ul>
077 *
078 * @since 10.0.0
079 */
080public abstract sealed class CsrfTokens {
081
082   /** Size in bytes of a token, of a pad, and of the minimum HMAC key. */
083   private static final int TOKEN_BYTES = 32;
084
085   /** Length of a masked token on the wire: pad and masked token, hex-encoded. */
086   private static final int MASKED_LENGTH = TOKEN_BYTES * 4;
087
088   /**
089    * The session id that a request with no session is HMAC'd under.
090    *
091    * <p>
092    * It contains a NUL character.  A session id travels as a cookie value or URL parameter, and neither can carry
093    * a control character, so no container-issued id can ever equal it and no real session's token can match the
094    * dummy HMAC.
095    */
096   private static final String NO_SESSION_ID = "no-session\u0000";
097
098   private static final String HMAC = "HmacSHA256";
099
100   private static final HexFormat HEX = HexFormat.of();
101
102   /** Shared CSPRNG for keys and pads; {@link SecureRandom} is thread-safe. */
103   private static final SecureRandom RANDOM = new SecureRandom();
104
105   private CsrfTokens() {}
106
107   /**
108    * A per-session strategy keyed by 32 fresh random bytes.
109    *
110    * <p>
111    * Each call returns a strategy with its own key, so tokens from two instances never cross-verify.  Use
112    * {@link PerSession#key(byte[])} to share one key across a cluster.
113    *
114    * @return A new per-session strategy.
115    */
116   public static PerSession perSession() {
117      var key = new byte[TOKEN_BYTES];
118      RANDOM.nextBytes(key);
119      return new PerSession(key);
120   }
121
122   /**
123    * A per-process strategy holding one freshly generated token.
124    *
125    * @return A new per-process strategy.
126    */
127   public static CsrfTokens perProcess() {
128      return perProcess(SynchronizerToken.generate());
129   }
130
131   /**
132    * A per-process strategy holding the given token.
133    *
134    * <p>
135    * The token's value must be exactly 64 lower-case hex characters (32 bytes), which is what
136    * {@link SynchronizerToken#generate()} produces.  Any other value is refused rather than stretched or hashed
137    * into shape: a passphrase is not a secret of the required strength, and quietly accepting one would hide that.
138    *
139    * @param token The process token.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
140    * @return A new per-process strategy.
141    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If {@code token} is <jk>null</jk> or its value is not 64 lower-case hex
142    *    characters.
143    */
144   public static CsrfTokens perProcess(SynchronizerToken token) {
145      reqnn("token", token);
146      var v = token.value();
147      if (! isLowerHex(v, TOKEN_BYTES * 2))
148         throw iaex("Argument 'token' must hold 64 lower-case hex characters, as SynchronizerToken.generate() produces.");
149      return new PerProcess(HEX.parseHex(v));
150   }
151
152   /**
153    * The expected 32-byte token for this request.
154    *
155    * <p>
156    * Never <jk>null</jk>.  For a per-session strategy with no session, this is the dummy HMAC, which no presented
157    * value can match.
158    *
159    * @param req The request.
160    * @param create Whether a per-session strategy may create a session.  A per-process strategy ignores it and
161    *    never touches the session.
162    * @return A new array holding the expected token.
163    */
164   abstract byte[] expected(HttpServletRequest req, boolean create);
165
166   /**
167    * Masks a token for one embed, under a fresh pad.
168    *
169    * @param token The 32-byte token from {@link #expected(HttpServletRequest, boolean)}.
170    * @return 128 lower-case hex characters, different on every call.
171    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If {@code token} is not 32 bytes.
172    */
173   final String mask(byte[] token) {
174      reqnn("token", token);
175      if (token.length != TOKEN_BYTES)
176         throw iaex("Argument 'token' must be %s bytes.", TOKEN_BYTES);
177      var pad = new byte[TOKEN_BYTES];
178      RANDOM.nextBytes(pad);
179      var out = Arrays.copyOf(pad, TOKEN_BYTES * 2);
180      for (var i = 0; i < TOKEN_BYTES; i++)
181         out[TOKEN_BYTES + i] = (byte)(pad[i] ^ token[i]);
182      return HEX.formatHex(out);
183   }
184
185   /**
186    * Whether a presented masked value carries the expected token.
187    *
188    * <p>
189    * The shape is checked first and does not depend on the secret.  A malformed value, including <jk>null</jk>,
190    * is <jk>false</jk>, never an exception.
191    *
192    * @param presented The value from the request header.  Can be <jk>null</jk>.
193    * @param expected The 32-byte token from {@link #expected(HttpServletRequest, boolean)}.
194    * @return <jk>true</jk> if {@code presented} unmasks to {@code expected}.
195    */
196   final boolean verify(String presented, byte[] expected) {
197      if (! isLowerHex(presented, MASKED_LENGTH))
198         return false;
199      return MessageDigest.isEqual(unmask(HEX.parseHex(presented)), expected);
200   }
201
202   /** Reverses {@link #mask(byte[])}: XORs the second half of {@code masked} with the pad in the first half. */
203   private static byte[] unmask(byte[] masked) {
204      var out = new byte[TOKEN_BYTES];
205      for (var i = 0; i < TOKEN_BYTES; i++)
206         out[i] = (byte)(masked[i] ^ masked[TOKEN_BYTES + i]);
207      return out;
208   }
209
210   /** Whether {@code s} is exactly {@code length} characters of lower-case hex. */
211   private static boolean isLowerHex(String s, int length) {
212      if (s == null || s.length() != length)
213         return false;
214      for (var i = 0; i < length; i++) {
215         var c = s.charAt(i);
216         if ((c < '0' || c > '9') && (c < 'a' || c > 'f'))
217            return false;
218      }
219      return true;
220   }
221
222   /**
223    * The per-session strategy: the token is <c>HMAC-SHA256(key, UTF-8(sessionId))</c>.
224    *
225    * <p>
226    * Thread-safe.  Only the key bytes are held; a {@link Mac} is created per computation.
227    */
228   public static final class PerSession extends CsrfTokens {
229
230      private final byte[] key;
231
232      private PerSession(byte[] key) {
233         this.key = key;
234      }
235
236      /**
237       * A strategy like this one, keyed by the given bytes.
238       *
239       * <p>
240       * For a cluster, where every node must accept every node's tokens.  The key <b>must</b> be output of a
241       * cryptographically secure random generator, such as 32 bytes from {@link SecureRandom}, kept in a secret
242       * store.  A passphrase or other human-chosen value is not a key, and this method cannot tell the difference.
243       *
244       * <p>
245       * The array is copied, so later changes to it have no effect.  This instance is unchanged.
246       *
247       * @param value The key.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>, and must be at least 32 bytes.
248       * @return A new strategy using {@code value} as its key.
249       * @throws IllegalArgumentException If {@code value} is <jk>null</jk> or shorter than 32 bytes.
250       */
251      public PerSession key(byte[] value) {
252         reqnn("value", value);
253         if (value.length < TOKEN_BYTES)
254            throw iaex("Argument 'value' must be at least %s bytes.", TOKEN_BYTES);
255         return new PerSession(value.clone());
256      }
257
258      @Override /* CsrfTokens */
259      byte[] expected(HttpServletRequest req, boolean create) {
260         var id = sessionId(req, create);
261         return hmac(id == null ? NO_SESSION_ID : id);
262      }
263
264      private static String sessionId(HttpServletRequest req, boolean create) {
265         try {
266            var s = req.getSession(create);
267            return s == null ? null : s.getId();
268         } catch (IllegalStateException e) {
269            // The session was invalidated, or the response is committed and a session can no longer be created.
270            return null;
271         }
272      }
273
274      private byte[] hmac(String id) {
275         try {
276            var mac = Mac.getInstance(HMAC);
277            mac.init(new SecretKeySpec(key, HMAC));
278            return mac.doFinal(id.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
279         } catch (GeneralSecurityException e) {
280            throw isex(e, "%s is not available.", HMAC);
281         }
282      }
283
284      /**
285       * Returns a description that does <b>not</b> include the key.
286       *
287       * @return A key-free description.
288       */
289      @Override /* Object */
290      public String toString() { return "CsrfTokens.perSession(key=<redacted>)"; }
291   }
292
293   /**
294    * The per-process strategy: one 32-byte token for every request.
295    */
296   private static final class PerProcess extends CsrfTokens {
297
298      private final byte[] token;
299
300      private PerProcess(byte[] token) {
301         this.token = token;
302      }
303
304      @Override /* CsrfTokens */
305      byte[] expected(HttpServletRequest req, boolean create) {
306         return token.clone();
307      }
308
309      /**
310       * Returns a description that does <b>not</b> include the token.
311       *
312       * @return A token-free description.
313       */
314      @Override /* Object */
315      public String toString() { return "CsrfTokens.perProcess(token=<redacted>)"; }
316   }
317}
